# lnurlcash-kit (Python)

LNURLcash (LUD-25) bearer note client for Python 3.10+. MIT.

pip install lnurlcash-kit

## What this is

LNURLcash notes are LUD-03 withdrawRequest links whose k1 IS the asset:
lnurlw://mint.example/w?k1=<spend>&amount=<msat>. Whoever knows the k1 can
spend it. Amounts are ALWAYS integer milli-satoshis.

LUD-25 (luds 6e865b1): every note is a BIP-341 taproot output key Q, named
cp1<Q>, filed by the mint under hex(Q). A k1 is a SPEND of it:
  64 hex    a bearer note's preimage: short form of the cw1 for the leaf
            OP_SHA256 <h> OP_EQUAL under the BIP-341 NUMS key. Signs nothing,
            so it spends at ANY mint holding the note
  ck1       Q || BIP-340 sig over the key-path sighash of a fixed transaction
            whose prevout is tagged_hash("LNURLcash/mint", domain). Spends at
            THAT mint only. Signing and verifying need the mint's domain
  cw1       leaf, control block, witness; Q recomputed from the control block
An output (p1/p2, a lookup's p, a mint comment) is a cp1 or a bearer note's
hex h = sha256(preimage), the short form of its cp1. note_id_of(k1) is hex(Q),
NOT sha256(k1). Domains: any URL or bare host, reduced to the lowercase
hostname (no scheme, no port) by spend_domain_of.

Draft spec: https://github.com/lnurl/luds/pull/301
Seed derivation, shares (cx1), registration proofs and the address fee are LUD-26
(luds 25.md and 26.md, through 92e430f), graded by lnurlcash-conformance 0.16.2.
Reference mint: https://github.com/dni/lnurl-mint

## Core API

from lnurlcash_kit import LnurlcashClient, AsyncLnurlcashClient

client = LnurlcashClient(timeout=30.0, offline=False, rng=generate_note_secret,
                         policy=Policy(), mutation_retries=1)
Policy(require_signatures=False, require_mint_pubkey=True) is the default.

client.fetch_note_info(url) -> WithdrawRequestInfo(callback, k1, max_withdrawable, mint_pubkey, signature)
client.rotate_note(callback, k1) -> RotateResult(k1, signature)
client.split_note(callback, k1s, amount_msat) -> SplitResult(k1, change, signature, change_signature)
client.merge_notes(callback, k1s) -> RotateResult
client.melt_note(callback, k1, bolt11) -> MeltResult(pr, verify)
client.settle_note(base_url, k1, expected_msat, sig) -> (k1, amount_msat, sig, callback)
client.probe_burned_note(url) -> 'live' | 'gone' | 'unknown'
client.fetch_pay_request(url) / request_invoice(cb, msat) / fetch_invoice_verification(url)
client.fetch_mint_address(url)

verify_note_signature(k1, domain, amount_msat, sig, mint_pubkey_hex) -> Certification
  checks k1 opens its Q at domain, then the cs1 over domain and hex(Q); falls
  back to hex(Q) with no domain (CERTIFIED_OVER_LEGACY_Q, before luds 92abbb3)
  and a bearer note's h (CERTIFIED_OVER_HASH, a pre-taproot mint). Only
  NOT_CERTIFIED is falsy
verify_note_url(note_url, mint_pubkey) -> (amount_msat | None, Certification)
resolve_note_input(text) / resolve_mint_input(text) / resolve_lnurl_input(text)
parse_mint_fee(metadata) / apply_mint_fee(gross, fee) / gross_up_for_mint_fee(net, fee)
  MintFee(base_fee_msat, fee_ppm, address_fee_msat): LUD-26's third value; the
  token is found anywhere in text/plain and its values end at whitespace;
  "Mint fees: 0,0,21000" is an address fee alone
internal_transfer_request(pay_request, note_domain, k1, amount_msat) -> Request
  LUD-26: send a WHOLE note to a Lightning Address's callback at the note's own
  mint (the address's withdrawLink must be on note_domain, else RequestRefused
  before anything is sent). parse_internal_transfer(body) reads the answer

AsyncLnurlcashClient has the identical surface with await.

For a different HTTP stack use lnurlcash_kit.protocol directly: each function
returns Request(url, parse, new_secrets) and performs no I/O.

## Rules an implementation MUST follow

1. max_withdrawable from fetch_note_info is the ONLY authoritative value. The
   `amount` in a note URL is an unverified claim.
2. On rotate/split/merge the WALLET generates the replacement secret and
   discloses only its public name (a bearer h, or a cp1). Never accept a
   service-supplied k1. A ck1 is per mint: sign it for the mint's domain.
3. Catch AmbiguousMutation, PERSIST err.new_secrets before anything else, then
   call probe_burned_note. Treating it as failure destroys money the service
   may already have minted.
4. RequestRefused means nothing was sent - safe to treat as a no-op.
5. A melt's OK means IN FLIGHT, not spent. NotePending means retry, not spent.
5b. A mint SHOULD certify every note with a cs1 over hex(Q), a bearer note
   included. A rotate/split/merge to an output named by a cp1 (p1, or p2 for
   a split's change) MUST return its cs1 in c (c2 for the change; a pre-50d740a mint's sig/sig2
   are still read, never sent) - this
   library's rule, stricter than LUD-25's SHOULD - and a missing one raises
   UnverifiableNote WHATEVER the policy says. An output named by a bearer h
   may come back with signature None from a mint with no signer.
   UnverifiableNote means the mutation LANDED, so keep its secrets (empty
   after a *_with_hash call: the caller already holds that key).
   Policy(require_signatures=True) demands a certificate for a bearer h
   output too. Policy(require_mint_pubkey=True), the default, refuses a
   withdrawRequest with no valid mintPubkey.
5c. A retried rotate/split/merge MUST be answered by the service as a replay of
   the original success, so a client re-sends one whose answer was lost
   (mutation_retries, default 1) and usually completes it. NEVER a melt. The
   IDENTICAL request goes out: the replay is matched on the notes the k1s
   open, p1, p2 and amount, so a fresh secret would make it a different
   mutation.
6. Rotate immediately after claiming a minted note: the mint generated that
   preimage, and LUD-21 verify exposes it to anyone who saw the invoice.
7. Never log note URLs. The spend is in the query string.
8. Never branch on exception message text. Branch on the class.

## Errors

RequestRefused     nothing sent, note untouched
ServiceRejected    processed and refused (definitive)
  NotePending      a melt is in flight on this k1 - retry
UnverifiableNote   the mutation LANDED without a certificate it owed: for an
                   output named by cp1, or by a bearer h under
                   require_signatures=True. The note is REAL; carries
                   .new_secrets - persist them
new_secrets_of(err) the secrets carried by ANY exception that could describe a
                   mutation the service applied: ambiguous, unverifiable, spent
                   or unknown
  NoteSpent        authoritative: already burned
  NoteUnknown      service does not recognise it
                   LUD-25's exact "already in use" (a burned note, or an output
                   that is somebody's already) is NoteSpent, so a mutation's
                   fresh secrets stay attached; is_already_in_use(err) matches
                   it in either reading, and a recovery scan counts it as used
  OutputInUse      lnurl-mint's older "Output already in use.": a p1/p2 is
                   taken. Nothing burned; name a fresh output
AmbiguousMint      outcome UNKNOWN - assume nothing
  AmbiguousMutation  carries .new_secrets - persist them
ProtocolError      a non-mutating response did not match the spec

## Conformance

https://github.com/lnurlcash/lnurlcash-conformance

Seed derivation (LUD-26, plain BIP-32):
derive_cash_root(seed) -> CashNode              BIP-32 m/139'
derive_service_root(root, domain) -> CashNode   S = m/139'/d1/d2/d3/d4, d1..d4 =
  HMAC-SHA256(privkey at m/139'/0, domain)[0..16] as 4 RAW big-endian uint32.
  domain is a URL, note URL or host reduced to its lowercase hostname, NO port.
  RAW: BIP-32 reads >= 2^31 as hardened, so ~half the levels are, decided by
  the domain. NEVER mask the top bit, NEVER harden all four - either derives a
  different tree and restores nothing, silently.
  Below S: S/a'/0/i wallet, S/a'/1/i change, S/a'/2/n' share n (its cx1),
  S/a'/2/n'/i note i of share n, credited by the SERVICE. a and n hardened,
  i < 2^31. A note's sk is the private key at its path, Q = x(sk*G).
derive_cash_domain_node(root, host) -> CashNode  the same walk over the host
  AS STORED (port included): the superseded tweak's node, not LUD-26's S.
Bearer preimages are plain randomness (generate_note_secret), not seed-derived.
cash_node_to_hex / cash_node_from_hex   privateKey || chainCode, 64 bytes
derive_cash_child(node, raw_uint32)     BIP-32 CKDpriv, for checking this
  library against BIP-32's own vectors
derive_cash_child_pub(pubkey33, chain_code, index) -> (pubkey33, chain_code)
  BIP-32 CKDpub; a hardened index is refused. cash_node_public_key(node) -> 33 bytes
derive_note_root / derive_note_secret   LEGACY pre-spec HMAC scheme. Do not
  mint under it; still scanned so old notes stay findable.
build_note_info_url_by_hash(link, h) / note_info_by_hash_request(link, h)
  the ?p= informational GET (h a cp1 or a bearer h), so a restore walk keeps
  spends off the wire. Unknown and BURNED are one answer.

Spends (lnurlcash_kit.spend, lnurlcash_kit.recoverable):
verify_spend(k1, domain) -> VerifiedSpend(output_key, legacy, unevaluated) | None
  opens which Q at this mint, as a mint would, time claims aside. legacy: an
  old ck1 (fixed message, or 65-byte ECDSA) - rotate it. unevaluated: a cw1
  whose leaf is not a bearer hashlock - structure, Q and leaf rules only
decode_spend(k1) -> Spend(kind: SpendKind, output_key, signature, script_path) | None
note_id_of(k1) -> hex(Q) | None   compare notes by this, NEVER by k1. Names,
  does not verify. fetch_note_info's echo check verifies at the note's domain
note_lookup_of(k1) -> a bearer preimage's h, else cp1<Q>; for note_info_by_hash_request
spend_domain_of(url or host) -> lowercase hostname
spend_prevout(domain), spend_sig_msg(Q, domain, locktime, sequence, leaf=None),
  key_path_sighash(Q, domain), script_path_sighash(Q, domain, leaf, lt, seq)
  SIGHASH_DEFAULT, input 0, hand-rolled; spec vector 3 pins every field
tap_leaf_hash(script, version=0xc0), taproot_tweak(P, merkle_root=b"") ->
  (Q, odd_y), output_key_of(script, control_block) -> Q | None (merkle fold,
  tweak, parity CHECKED), is_x_only_point(x), NUMS_KEY, TAPLEAF_VERSION
bearer_leaf(h), bearer_note(h) -> BearerNote(output_key, control_block, leaf),
  bearer_note_id(hex h) -> hex(Q), bearer_cw1(preimage) -> the full cw1
Cw1(locktime, sequence, script, control_block, witness); encode_cw1 /
  decode_cw1 (structure only) / is_cw1 / output_key_of_cw1. Big-endian
  u32 u32 (u16 len item)*
check_leaf_policy(version, script) -> reason | None  refuses leaf version !=
  0xc0 and any OP_SUCCESSx outside pushed data
check_time_claim(locktime, sequence, now, locked_at) -> reason | None  the
  mint's clock rules; custodial, never trustless
No script interpreter.

Key-path notes and the wire values (lnurlcash_kit.recoverable):
All of cp1, ck1, cw1, cs1, cx1 are bech32m, no 90-char limit, upper case fine,
mixed case refused. Decoders return None, never raise.
encode_cp1/ck1(bytes) -> str       decode_cp1/ck1(str) -> bytes | None
  decode_cp1 refuses a key that is not a curve point
  encode_ck1 takes the 96 bytes Q || sig only; decode_ck1/is_ck1 also accept
  the LEGACY 65-byte recoverable-ECDSA ck1 so an old note can be rotated
encode_cs1_with_amount(amount_msat, sig) / decode_cs1_with_amount -> Cs1
  CURRENT: HRP is "cs" plus the BOLT11 amount suffix; signature covers
  LNURLcash:<amount_msat>:<hex(Q)>.
encode_cs1/decode_cs1/is_cs1 are LEGACY fixed-HRP only.
decode_any_cs1/is_any_cs1 accept either certificate during migration.
Cx1(chain_code, pubkey) with .pubkey_x_only: a share's xpub, 65 bytes in
  BIP-32's order (chain code, then the 33-byte compressed point), 113 chars.
encode_cx1(cx1) / decode_cx1(str) -> Cx1 | None   None for the old 64-byte
  shape and for a key that is not a compressed curve point
is_cp1 / is_ck1 / is_cw1 / is_cs1_with_amount / is_cx1(str) -> bool
NotePath.wallet(a, i) / .change(a, i) / .for_share(a, n, i); CHAIN_WALLET=0,
  CHAIN_CHANGE=1, CHAIN_SHARE=2
derive_note_key(S, path) -> NoteKey(secret_key, pubkey (33, shows y parity),
  output_key = Q)
derive_share_node(S, account, share) -> CashNode   S/a'/2/n'; its private key
  signs the share's registration proofs
cash_node_to_cx1(node) -> Cx1   hand this out, never the node
derive_note_pubkey(cx1, i) -> 32-byte Q   CKDpub, watch-only: what a mint
  credits a registered share with. Hardened i refused; an unusable i (~2^-127)
  raises ProtocolError: use the next
SUPERSEDED, read only, for finding and sweeping old notes (never register or mint):
  legacy_branch_node(root, host_as_stored), legacy_cx1_of(node) -> LegacyCx1
  (x(P), chain_code; encode_legacy_cx1 / decode_legacy_cx1, the 64-byte shape),
  legacy_derive_note_pubkey(legacy_cx1, purpose, i),
  legacy_derive_note_secret_key(node, purpose, i); purpose is
  LEGACY_PURPOSE_WALLET=0, _CHANGE=1, _LIGHTNING_ADDRESS=2, or None for the
  scheme before purposes. t = tagged_hash("LNURLcash/derive", P || chain_code
  [|| ser32_be(purpose)] || ser32_be(i)) mod n.
sign_note_ownership(sk, domain) -> 96 bytes Q || BIP-340 sig over
  key_path_sighash(Q, domain), zero aux_rand: one deterministic ck1 per mint
recover_note_ownership_pubkey(payload, domain) -> NoteOwnership(pubkey_x_only,
  legacy) | None   the domain's sighash, else the old fixed messages
  (legacy); a 65-byte ECDSA payload is recovered (legacy)
Registration proofs (LUD-26), BIP-340 by the SHARE's own key over sha256 of
  LNURLcash:register:<domain>:<username>:<cx1>
  LNURLcash:update:<domain>:<username>:<new cx1>   (by the key on file; a PUT
    also carries a register proof by the new share)
  LNURLcash:unregister:<domain>:<username>         (no cx1)
  username lowercased; cx1 required for register/update, refused for unregister.
address_proof_message(action, domain, username, cx1=None) -> str
address_proof_digest(action, domain, username, cx1=None) -> sha256 of it
sign_address_proof(share_sk, action, domain, username, cx1=None) -> 64 bytes
verify_address_proof(signer_cx1, sig, action, domain, username, cx1=None) -> bool
  the SERVICE's check, against x(P) of the signer's cx1; never raises
Wire: a spend goes anywhere a k1 does (note URL, fetch_note_info, rotate,
  split, merge, melt). An output (cp1 or bearer h) goes as p1/p2 from the
  *_with_hash calls, p on a lookup, the comment on a mint invoice (a bearer h
  also as h). An off-curve cp1 is refused before sending.
Certificates (lnurlcash_kit.signature), cs1 over
  "LNURLcash:<domain>:<amount_msat>:<hex(Q)>", recovery id LAST (0 to 3):
  verify_note_signature(k1, domain, amount_msat, sig, mint_pubkey)
  verify_note_signature_hash(hex_q, domain, amount, cs1, pubkey) -> bool
    a watcher with no spend; current certificates only, a cs1 stating amount
  check_note_certificate(cp1_or_bearer_h, domain, amount, sig, pubkey)
    -> Certification   current, then the legacy messages
  verify_legacy_note_signature_hash(id, amount, sig, pubkey) -> bool
    "LNURLcash:<amount>:<id>" (no domain); raw hex / either recovery layout
  verify_note_url(note_url, mint_pubkey)
  -> Certification.CERTIFIED_OVER_Q | CERTIFIED_OVER_LEGACY_Q |
     CERTIFIED_OVER_HASH | NOT_CERTIFIED
  note_signature_message(k1, domain, amt), note_signature_message_for_hash(
    hex_id, domain, amt), the digest pair, and legacy_note_signature_message_
    for_hash / _digest_for_hash(id, amt): the messages over a note's hex id
derive_cash_master(seed) -> CashNode   BIP-32 master, for paths not named here
EXTENSION, not LUD-25/26: derive_nostr_cash_seed(sk) = HMAC-SHA256(key = sk,
  msg = "LNURLcash/nostr-seed"); derive_nostr_service_root(sk, domain) = S for
  that seed, LUD-26's tree unchanged. sk is the raw 32 bytes an nsec encodes.
